title: Newcastle’s Lewis Miley expected to return from leg injury within two weeks, Eddie Howe says
content:
Lewis Miley is expected to return to the Newcastle United squad within the next fortnight after suffering complications to the leg injury he picked up in the team’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in January.

The England Under-21 international struggled to bend his knee in the immediate aftermath of Newcastle’s Champions League match in France but the injury was diagnosed as a dead leg and he made a non-playing appearance on the substitutes’ bench for their next game away to Liverpool.

What should have been a routine problem failed to clear up and Miley has now not played for eight fixtures in all competitions.

Eddie Howe admitted in his press conference ahead of Newcastle’s home game against Everton that they are taking every precaution with the 19-year-old midfielder, with the fear that he could miss the rest of the season if he is rushed back.

“We’ve just been advised with Lewis to be really careful with this injury,” Howe said. “It was a dead leg, so a knock and usually with a knock of that type, it’s maybe a couple of days and you’re back, but there was a little bit of muscle disruption.

“He’s had a couple of injections and I think he’s got one more to come. I’ve been saying a couple of weeks for a while, but we’re looking at a couple of weeks with Lewis. Because I think if we don’t get the management of this injury right, it could rule him out for the season. We’re being careful to hopefully get him back in a good place.”

Howe was also asked how Miley, who has also played at right-back for Newcastle this season, is dealing with his enforced absence.

“Typical Lewis,” the head coach said. “Not a massive amount of emotion, but that’s a strength. He goes about his work in a really good way. I’m sure behind the scenes he’s disappointed because he was in such a good place.

“He was playing really well in whatever position we asked him to play and he was integral to what we were doing. And he also gave us a lot more choice and options to play different ways. So he’s been a huge miss and we’re desperate to get him back, but we have to respect the injury timescale.”
